<problem>
A finite set $A\subset\mathbb N$ is a Sidon set if the differences $a-a'$ with $a\neq a'$, $a,a'\in A$, are pairwise distinct. A finite set $B\subset\mathbb Z$ whose elements are pairwise distinct modulo $v\ge 1$ is a perfect difference set modulo $v$ if every nonzero residue class modulo $v$ equals $b-b'$ for exactly one ordered pair of distinct $b,b'\in B$. Say $A$ extends if $A\subseteq B$ for some $v\ge1$ and some perfect difference set $B$ modulo $v$. For $k,N\in\mathbb N$ let $S_k(N)$ be the number of $k$-element Sidon subsets of $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$ and $E_k(N)$ the number of those that extend, and put $c_k=\limsup_{N\to\infty}E_k(N)/S_k(N)\in[0,1]$. (1) Is $c_k<1$ for some $k$, and does $c_k\to0$ as $k\to\infty$? (2) Is $E_4(N)=S_4(N)$ for all $N$, i.e. does every Sidon set with at most four elements extend?
</problem>

<solution>
Setting. Write v=q^2+q+1 and |B|=q+1 for a perfect difference set (PDS) B modulo v. Translating B and re-choosing integer representatives shows: A extends iff there is v and a PDS B mod v with (A mod v) ⊆ (B mod v); in particular A must be Sidon modulo v and |A| ≤ q+1.

Reformulation for Singer sets. Identify G = F_{q^3}^*/F_q^* (cyclic of order v) with the points of PG(2,q). The Singer set of a generator α of G is B_α={a : α^a ∈ L} for a line L; translates and multiplier images of Singer sets are all of this form (changing α to α^t multiplies B by t^{-1}). Hence A embeds in a Singer-type PDS mod v iff for some generator α of G the points {α^a : a∈A} are collinear in PG(2,q), i.e. {α^a} spans an F_q-subspace of F_{q^3} of dimension ≤ 2.

Rigorous results.
(1) k ≤ 2: every Sidon set extends. For A={a,a+d} take a prime p with v=p^2+p+1>d and a Singer set B; d≢0 so d≡b−b' for exactly one pair; use B−b'+a with representatives a, a+d.
(2) k=3: A={0,d_1,d_1+d_2} embeds in a Singer-type PDS mod v iff m=(d_1+d_2)d_1^{-1} mod v admits β∈F_{q^3}\F_q with β^m ∈ F_q+F_qβ. E.g. m=3 always works for q=p>3 (β a root of an irreducible X^3−wX−u), so {0,d,3d} extends; m=p,p^2 work when p≡1 (mod 3); m∈{2,1/2,−1} are impossible for all q, matching exactly the non-Sidon configurations {0,d,2d} etc. Expected number of admissible generators per q is ≍ q^2, but a lower bound for each m needs character sums of degree ~q^2 over F_{q^3}, beyond the Weil bound.
(3) Multiplier obstruction. Let A⊆B, B a PDS mod v=q^2+q+1, p a prime dividing q, so pB≡B+s (Hall). If a_1−a_3=p(a_2−a_4) in A with a_1≠a_3, then Sidon-ness of the p-fixed translate B'=B+c forces (p−1)c≡a_1−pa_2, and ⋃_{j≥0} p^j(A+c) (mod v) must be Sidon mod v with at most q+1 elements. Example: A={0,1,3}, v=21, q=4, p=2: c=1 and the orbit {1,2,4,8,16} has 8−1≡2−16 (mod 21), so {0,1,3} is contained in no PDS modulo 21 (it is contained in {1,2,4} mod 7). Similarly A⊇{0,1,p} embedded with q=p^a forces ord_v(p)=3a≤q and {0}∪{p^j} Sidon mod v.

Heuristic count. For a fixed k-set A and given q, collinearity of the k points α^a is k−2 roughly independent conditions of probability ≈1/q each, over φ(v)≈q^2 generators: expected number of Singer embeddings mod v is ≍ q^{4−k}. Summing over prime powers q: for k≤4 (and k=5) the sum diverges, so failure probability ∏(1−c q^{4−k})=0 — supporting a YES to (2); for k≥6 the sum converges, so a positive proportion of Sidon k-sets should not extend (c_k<1), and since Σ_q q^{4−k}→0 (and q+1≥k kills small q), c_k→0.

What is missing for full proofs: (a) for (2) an existence theorem giving one good q per 4-set (a lower bound for generators α with four prescribed powers collinear — a degree ~q^2 character sum over F_{q^3}); (b) for (1) control over all PDS, including hypothetical non-Singer ones, for arbitrarily large v; the multiplier theorem constrains only one v at a time.

Answer (with these caveats): (1) Expected yes: c_k<1 for all large k (heuristically k≥6) and c_k→0. (2) Expected yes: every Sidon set with at most four elements extends. Proved here: k≤2 extend; exact collinearity reformulation; explicit extension of some 3-sets (e.g. {0,d,3d}); explicit non-extension of specific sets for specific moduli via multipliers ({0,1,3} ⊄ any PDS mod 21).
</solution>
